facts.summary: Michigan's minimum wage is $13.73 per hour effective January 1, 2026, higher than the federal $7.25.
facts.citation: Improved Workforce Opportunity Wage Act, MCL 408.934
facts.sourceAgency: Michigan Dept of Labor & Economic Opportunity (LEO), Wage & Hour Division
facts.notes: Rate is scheduled to rise to $15.00/hr on Jan 1, 2027; confirm no mid-year adjustment before relying on figure.

facts.summary: Michigan requires overtime at 1.5x after 40 hours in a 7-day workweek with no daily overtime rule, and uses FLSA-based exemptions, so it tracks federal law.
facts.citation: Improved Workforce Opportunity Wage Act, MCL 408.934a
facts.sourceAgency: Michigan Dept of Labor & Economic Opportunity (LEO), Wage & Hour Division
facts.notes: Michigan does not set a state salary floor separate from the federal FLSA salary-level test; exemptions mirror the FLSA.

facts.summary: Michigan's Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act protects several classes beyond the federal set, including sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, height, weight, familial status, and marital status.
facts.citation: Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act, Act 453 of 1976, MCL 37.2202
facts.sourceAgency: Michigan Legislature / Michigan Dept of Civil Rights (MDCR)
facts.notes: These are in addition to religion, race, color, national origin, age, and sex, which overlap with federal protections.

facts.summary: The Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act defines an employer as anyone with 1 or more employees, far below the federal Title VII threshold of 15.
facts.sourceAgency: Michigan Legislature / Michigan Dept of Civil Rights (MDCR)

facts.value: Persons with Disabilities Civil Rights Act (PWDCRA)
facts.summary: Michigan's Persons with Disabilities Civil Rights Act separately prohibits disability discrimination and requires accommodation, enforced by MDCR alongside the federal ADA.
facts.citation: Persons with Disabilities Civil Rights Act, Act 220 of 1976, MCL 37.1101 et seq.
facts.notes: PWDCRA applies more broadly than the federal ADA's 15-employee threshold; verify specific accommodation provisions in MCL 37.1102/37.1210 if precise language is needed.

facts.summary: Michigan's Whistleblowers' Protection Act bars retaliation against employees who report suspected legal violations to a public body, but a civil action must be filed within 90 days.
facts.citation: Whistleblowers' Protection Act, Act 469 of 1980, MCL 15.362-15.363
facts.notes: The 90-day limitations period (MCL 15.363) is strict and shorter than most other Michigan employment deadlines.

facts.summary: A minimum wage or overtime complaint under the Improved Workforce Opportunity Wage Act must be filed within 3 years; unpaid-wages/fringe-benefit claims under Act 390 have a shorter 12-month administrative filing window.
facts.citation: Improved Workforce Opportunity Wage Act, MCL 408.934; Payment of Wages and Fringe Benefits Act, MCL 408.481
facts.sourceAgency: Michigan Dept of Labor & Economic Opportunity (LEO), Wage & Hour Division
facts.notes: Deadlines differ by claim type: min wage/overtime = 3 years; Payment of Wages & Fringe Benefits Act administrative complaint = 12 months. Confirm which applies to a given claim.

facts.summary: A discrimination complaint must be filed with the Michigan Dept of Civil Rights within 180 days of the alleged act; a civil suit directly under Elliott-Larsen has a separate 3-year limitations period.
facts.citation: Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act, MCL 37.2602 (MDCR complaint procedures)
facts.notes: 180 days is the administrative MDCR filing window; the 3-year figure for direct court actions comes from Michigan case law, not a statute section, so treat it as guidance.
